title: Service Boundary Fidelity Transition Playbook
author: Dana Chen
body:
Summary
=======
This playbook defines the product and operational plan for transitioning tenant traffic across service boundaries as we introduce fidelity-tier boundaries and per-route fidelity controls. It consolidates product overview context, minimum viable requirements (PRD), a high-level design spec, a staged roadmap and themes, pricing and packaging implications, and release notes/communications to customers. The intent is to provide a single source of truth for product, engineering, and GTM teams executing the transition.

Goals
-----
- Ensure predictable user experience when fidelity boundaries are applied across service tiers.
- Provide clear SLOs and rollback criteria to protect revenue and quality.
- Minimize customer friction through phased rollout and transparent billing mapping.
- Enable platform teams to implement controls without ad-hoc service changes.

Scope and non-goals
-------------------
In scope:
- Per-route fidelity controls exposed in the Redwood API and Console.
- Runtime routing from hosted->dedicated/private variants when fidelity conflicts arise.
- Billing mapping from fidelity tiers to existing token/credit models.
- Telemetry and QA/eval capture for quality regressions.

Out of scope:
- New model variant marketplace onboarding flow (separate PRD).
- Deep kernel/runtime optimizations for quantization (runtime/infra teams own).

Product requirements (PRD) — minimum viable
-----------------------------------------
1) API surface
   - Add `fidelity` optional field on generation and embeddings routes (enum: low, standard, high, ultra).
   - Backwards compatibility: default behavior = `standard` when omitted.
   - Per-route account config: owners can set a `fidelity_cap` and `fidelity_floor` in Console and via the admin API.

2) Billing & metering
   - Each fidelity tier maps to a multiplier on token-based billing: low=0.6x, standard=1x, high=1.6x, ultra=2.2x.
   - Credits and quota consumption must be visible in Console per-route and per-token class.

3) Guardrails and safety
   - Quality regression detection: sample 0.1% of requests with golden prompt sets (configurable per account).
   - Automatic rollback trigger if regression rate > 3% for 24h on a route or if customer complaint >= 5 in 7 days.

4) Rollout controls
   - Canary by tenant subset: 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% with manual approval gates.
   - Per-tenant opt-out window for 30 days after first enforcement.

Design summary (high-level)
---------------------------
- Control Plane: extend route configuration model with fidelity fields and pricing mapping. Console exposes UI and API endpoints.
- Data Plane / Runtime: route table contains (route_id, fidelity_cap, assigned_variant). Routing policy evaluates fidelity requirement then picks compatible model variant and runtime pool.
- Observability: add fidelity dimension to existing per-token metrics, latency histograms, cost attribution, and loss/regression dashboards.

Service boundary behaviors (examples)
------------------------------------
- If a request requests `ultra` but tenant `fidelity_cap` is `high`, the runtime will:
  1) If compatible higher-precision variant available on the same tier, serve it and bill at `high` pricing.
  2) Else, follow fallback policy (either downgrade to `high` or error depending on tenant policy).

Detailed config table (reference)
--------------------------------
| Field | Type | Description | Default | Owner |
| route.fidelity | enum | Requested fidelity level | standard | product |
| route.fidelity_cap | enum | Maximum fidelity allowed for route | ultra | product |
| route.fidelity_floor | enum | Minimum fidelity guaranteed | low | product |
| pricing.multiplier | float | Multiplier applied to token price for tier | see mapping | finance |

YAML example (route config)
---------------------------
```
route_id: sales-chat
fidelity: high
fidelity_cap: ultra
fidelity_floor: standard
billing_tag: per-tenant-abc
```

Rollout plan and timeline
-------------------------
Phase 0 — Engineering & QA (Weeks 0–6)
1. Implement API schema changes and Console mockups.
2. Runtime handling for fidelity flagging and fallback policies.
3. Integrate telemetry dimensions and create baseline dashboards.
4. Internal E2E tests with synthetic workloads and golden prompts.

Phase 1 — Beta customers (Weeks 7–12)
1. Invite 6 existing enterprise customers across industries (SaaS, fintech, healthcare).
2. Run 6-week controlled experiment: 10% of traffic opt-in.
3. Weekly quality reviews and billing reconciliation.

Phase 2 — Gradual ramp (Weeks 13–22)
1. Open to self-serve tenants with console opt-in.
2. Canary rollout for hosted regions (5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100%) with monitoring gates.
3. Publish pricing guidance and migration FAQ.

Phase 3 — Enforcement & defaults (Weeks 23+)
1. Make fidelity enforcement the default for new tenants.
2. Continue monitoring and runbook updates.

SLOs, metrics and alerting
--------------------------
Primary SLOs (product-facing)
- Fidelity correctness: 99.5% of requests are served with an allowed fidelity within 250ms decision time.
- Quality regression SLO: False positive regression triggers <= 1/month; regressions detected correctly >= 95%.

Operational metrics to instrument
- Per-route fidelity distribution (percent of tokens/requests by tier).
- Cost delta per-tenant week-over-week.
- Latency added by fidelity evaluation step.
- Golden set evaluation pass-rate and regression ratio.

Alerting configuration (examples)
- P0: Regression ratio > 3% for 24h on a route -> page SRE + oncall PM.
- P1: Billing multiplier mismatch detected for a tenant -> Slack alert and ticket.

Pricing and packaging implications
---------------------------------
- Introduce Fidelity Credits as a visible billing abstraction: customers can purchase bundles that guarantee `high` fidelity up to X tokens per month. Unused high-fidelity tokens do not rollover.
- Migration offers: 3-month introductory discount (20% off fidelity multipliers) for tenants who accept automated fidelity enforcement.
- Enterprise add-on: fidelity insurance that guarantees auto-rollbacks if quality drops (legal & finance approval required).

GTM and customer communications
------------------------------
- Documentation: Console help article and migration FAQ published at time of Beta open.
- Email cadence: initial invite -> onboarding guide -> 2-week status -> 30-day opt-out reminder.
- Sales enablement: one-pager mapping fidelity tiers to common customer workloads (search, summarization, code-gen).

Release notes (intended content for public release)
--------------------------------------------------
- Feature: Per-request fidelity control and per-route fidelity caps.
- Benefit: Lower cost options for latency-sensitive workloads and high-quality tiers for revenue-critical paths.
- Migration: Default remains unchanged; new console options available for interested customers.
- Known limitations: fidelity decisions will not be supported for streaming fallback during v1.0.

Rollback and incident playbook (short)
------------------------------------
1. Detect regression via golden-set or customer report.
2. If regression meets rollback criteria (see PRD), perform immediate rollback to previous fidelity mapping and notify customer.
3. Post-incident: run root cause analysis, update acceptance tests, and schedule hotfix if needed.
